statement: In the separately declared PLF 7.1 MoreStlc fix extension, t=fix(lambda x:Nat.x) has type Nat. Its unfolding step substitutes t for x in body x, giving t again. Every finite prefix can take another such step, so no normal value is reached along this infinite reduction. This is not a counterexample to the no-stuck safety property, and the fix rule is not silently added to the core STLC theorem.

statement: In the pure rank-one model, initial environment {x:alpha} receives substitution alpha=(beta->beta). Inferring let y=x yields tau=beta->beta while the current environment is {x:beta->beta}. Both free-variable sets are {beta}, so GEN quantifies their difference, the empty set. By contrast, an unrelated identity lambda z.z with fresh gamma outside that environment can receive forall gamma.gamma->gamma and independent use instantiations.

statement: A TypeScript 5.9.3 function takes xs:number[] and binds const v=xs[0] with strictNullChecks=true and noUncheckedIndexedAccess=true. Its value is statically number|undefined, so an unguarded toFixed() is rejected. Writing v!.toFixed() bypasses that static nullish restriction, but calling the emitted function with [] still reaches an undefined receiver and TypeError. A fresh v!==void 0 test before using that same stable value supplies a real guard.

The term let id=lambda x.x in let ignored=id true in id zero is accepted because each id occurrence instantiates its generalized scheme separately.
